result.title: How Fine-Tuning Objectives Shape Layer-Wise Information in LLM Hallucination Detection
result.summary: Under matched conditions, classifier-head fine-tuning (\textsc{cls}) paradigm consistently outperforms the LLM-as-Judge sequence-to-sequence (\textsc{s2s}) on binary hallucination detection. We trace this gap to the representations induced by the two objectives. Static analysis shows that \textsc{cls} learns a task-specific discriminative direction, pushing hidden states into a clear two-cluster geometry with stronger class separation and linearly decodable label information. By contrast, \textsc{s2s} relies on the pretrained language-modeling head to make decisions. This minimizes the pressure to reorganize representations, leaving the hidden states much closer to the pretrained backbone. Our analysis also reveals that the \textsc{cls} signal saturates before the final layer, after which upper layers form a plateau of statistically interchangeable and largely redundant representations. However, endpoint redundancy alone does not show whether these layers are dispensable during training. Further training-dynamics analysis reveals 1) a lower pretrained substrate, 2) a narrow upper-middle \textbf{InfoWindow} where task information emerges, and 3) a later-synchronizing upper plateau that mirrors this signal. This mechanism motivates us to remove layers above the InfoWindow. Truncating 31\% of the network leaves accuracy unchanged within seed noise on Qwen3-4B and 8B and cuts latency by $1.4\times$. The same depth fraction, fixed before any analysis of the target models, transfers to Llama-3.2-3B and Mistral-7B-v0.3, and the layer structure behind it reappears there and on QNLI and SST-2. We hope this helps guide efficient task-specific LLM design.

AI.brief_summary: 在匹配条件下比较分类头微调与 seq2seq 两种目标对 LLM 幻觉检测的影响，用层间表示几何与训练动态分析发现任务信息集中在中上层「InfoWindow」，并据此裁剪 31% 的层数，在保持精度的同时降低延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其层间探测、按深度定位任务信号涌现窗口并做冗余层截断的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态在哪些层生成、上层是否可省及动态计算成本；但研究对象是纯文本幻觉检测，不涉及多模态视觉推理。
